nodes.label: generate-schema.mjs provider-swap mechanism
nodes.rationale: Installed Prisma version only allows env() on url, not on datasource.provider itself, so the provider line must be swapped in a gitignored copy (schema.generated.prisma) rather than hand-edited per environment.

nodes.label: DATABASE_PROVIDER env var (postgresql default, sqlite for local dev)
simulate(geometry, materials, windows, weather, operation): TimeSeries
nodes.rationale: Frozen as the one pure function signature on day one: no database, no state, no I/O, so it runs unchanged in a browser Web Worker and in Node, and is cheap enough to call 2,000 times for the optimiser.

nodes.label: Conservation of energy: dT/dt = (Q_in - Q_out)/(m*c)
nodes.rationale: The one physical law the whole project is built on; the denominator m*c (thermal capacitance) is literally the problem statement — existing shelters have too little m*c and too much Q_out.

nodes.label: Material type (5 numbers: k, rho, c, alphaS, eps)
Window type (4 numbers: U, SHGC, tauVis, b0)
Surface geometry type (area, tilt, azimuth, layers, boundary)
Weather type (four/five 8760-length arrays)
nodes.rationale: Ladakh ships as a preset, not hardcoded logic — swapping the four arrays satisfies DRDO's 'other climatic regions' requirement at zero extra effort.

nodes.label: Thermal-electrical circuit analogy (T~V, Q~I, R, C, RC time constant)
nodes.rationale: Not a metaphor — the same differential equation as an RC low-pass filter, exploited directly in §5.5 to get a closed-form answer the numerical model can be tested against.

nodes.label: Shelter-as-graph node model (air, wall, surface, ground, storage, ambient/sky nodes)
The eleven energy pathways Q1-Q11
nodes.rationale: Q5/Q6/Q7 redistribute heat internally and never cross the system boundary; getting that distinction wrong is the single easiest way to break the energy-balance self-check.

nodes.label: Air density at altitude (§5.2)
nodes.rationale: At 3500 m air is ~65% as dense as sea level; every term involving air mass or movement (capacitance, infiltration, both convection coefficients) must use it — a judge from a high-altitude lab will ask about exactly this.

nodes.label: Ground albedo / snow reflection effect
nodes.rationale: Snow quadruples the reflected term (0.20 -> 0.80); a south wall above snowfield can receive more total irradiance in winter than summer, a strong region-specific pitch detail.

nodes.label: Conduction through walls — the heart of the engine (§5.5)
nodes.rationale: A wall modelled as one lump responds instantly; slicing it into a 1-D node chain is the only reason the engine can reproduce thermal lag and damping — the entire mechanism by which a passive shelter survives the night.

nodes.label: Exterior wall face boundary (wind convection + sky/ground radiation, §5.6)
Infrared radiation to the cold sky (Q4)
nodes.rationale: On a clear Ladakh night the sky behaves like a -44C sink, a 29K driving difference all night; a model without Q4 predicts comfortable nights that don't exist, and DRDO's DIHAR lab is headquartered in Leh.

nodes.label: Interior wall face boundary (direction-dependent convection + star node, §5.7)
nodes.rationale: The 4x asymmetry between floor-heats-room (4.04) and ceiling-heats-room (0.95) is real physics, not a fudge factor, and implies floor-based thermal mass beats ceiling-based mass in a direct-gain shelter.

nodes.label: Radiant star node for interior longwave exchange
nodes.rationale: Instead of an O(N^2) view-factor matrix, every surface talks to one fictitious hub node, O(N) links — the ISO 13790 5R1C approach.

nodes.label: Night insulation shutters (§5.8.1)
nodes.rationale: A quilted/EPS shutter cuts window losses ~70% for a few hundred rupees; the optimiser ranking this above triple glazing is both a headline pitch result and a genuinely deployable recommendation.

nodes.label: Air leakage / infiltration model (§5.9)
nodes.rationale: Infiltration is frequently the largest single night-time loss and by far the cheapest to fix (weatherstripping, a door gasket) — a genuinely actionable headline finding.

nodes.label: ACH responds to opening size (§5.9.1, C_leak knob)
nodes.rationale: Larger windows are also longer air-leak paths, not just bigger conduction holes; without this coupling sweeping window area has no clean optimum, breaking the tool's most important demo (question K-05).

nodes.label: ACH_min hard safety floor (§5.9.2)
nodes.rationale: Ladakhi shelters use unvented bukhari stoves; sealing a shelter without maintaining combustion air/exhaust recommends a carbon monoxide hazard, so the optimiser must never return a design below the floor, no matter the thermal score.

nodes.label: Floor-to-ground coupling, Kusuda-Achenbach soil temperature (§5.10)
nodes.rationale: In midwinter the ground sits well above air temperature (a heat source, not a sink) — why semi-buried/earth-bermed shelters perform well at altitude, a non-obvious result to show a judge.

nodes.label: Internal free heat gains (people, stove, livestock, §5.11)
nodes.rationale: Traditional Ladakhi houses stable animals under the living space as a distributed biological heater — a genuine vernacular strategy worth modelling as a toggleable gain.

nodes.label: The air node equation (§5.12) — the output curve
Effective air capacitance multiplier M=4
nodes.rationale: Bare room air's heat capacity is tiny; furniture, bedding, clothing and finishes respond within minutes and move with the air, so leaving them out makes the system numerically stiff and unrealistically twitchy.

nodes.label: PCM (phase change material) apparent heat capacity extension (§5.13)
Solver assembly: C*dT/dt = K*T + f(t), arrow matrix (§6)
Implicit (backward Euler) time stepping, non-negotiable (§6.2)
nodes.rationale: Explicit Euler requires Fourier number <=0.5 at every node; a thin insulation layer would force an impractically tiny timestep, so implicit stepping is required for stability.

nodes.label: Sign convention (§3, quoted verbatim from CONTRACTS.md §7.2)
Energy-balance residual definition (§4)
nodes.rationale: Normalised by E_gross, not E_in, because E_in normalisation degenerates for night-only reporting windows where gains are near zero; pass threshold residual < 0.001, asserted in CI on every preset.

nodes.label: Physical constants (§5, constants.ts)
nodes.rationale: KEROSENE_INR_PER_L=80 is flagged in its own comment as an assumption, not a sourced figure, and must stay editable in the UI.

nodes.label: Transposition: Liu & Jordan isotropic and HDKR (§9, solar/transposition.ts)
Shading, overhang profile-angle construction (§10, solar/shading.ts)
nodes.rationale: Both shading functions gate the beam component only, leaving diffuse/ground-reflected untouched by design; ceiling is overestimated gain on a deeply overhung surface, upgrade path is a sky-dome view-factor reduction.

nodes.label: Envelope meshing and transient conduction (§11, envelope/mesh.ts)
nodes.rationale: Nodes sit on every layer interface and both outer faces, so every edge lies wholly inside one material: the harmonic-mean interface formula becomes structurally inapplicable rather than merely satisfied, making the steady-state U-value analytically exact.

nodes.label: Exterior boundary (§13, surfaces/exterior.ts)
nodes.rationale: h_o is deliberately convective-only, not the McAdams combined 5.7+3.8v coefficient, because radiation to the sky is modelled explicitly and separately — using McAdams here would double-count Q4.

nodes.label: Infiltration, ventilation, calibration knobs (§16, loads/infiltration.ts)
nodes.rationale: ACH_MIN is enforced twice independently — in infiltration()/effectiveAch() and again in the optimiser's own constraint check — intentional redundancy, not a defect.

nodes.label: Discrete thermal storage nodes: water, rock, PCM (§20, storage/waterMass.ts)
air.ts:convectionAltitudeFactor
nodes.rationale: Convection assumed to scale with density^0.5 (mixed forced/natural regime), a simplification of Nusselt-Reynolds power-law scaling not measured at altitude; upgrade path is recalibrating the exponent against a high-altitude dataset.

nodes.label: loads/infiltration.ts:effectiveAch
nodes.rationale: ACH_PER_GLAZING_FRACTION (1.2 per unit glazing-area fraction) is a plausible, not calibrated, coupling — its own doc comment says to tune it if a measured blower-door figure for a real Ladakhi shelter ever becomes available.

nodes.label: loads/ground.ts:soilTemperature
nodes.rationale: SLAB_SOIL_CONDUCTANCE is a fixed equivalent soil resistance; upgrade to the full ISO 13370 perimeter/area method if ground losses ever dominate a result.

nodes.label: storage/pcm.ts:pcmEnthalpy (closed-form antiderivative)
nodes.rationale: A PCM node's ΔStored contribution must be pcmEnthalpy(T_end)-pcmEnthalpy(T_0), never C_j(T_end)*ΔT, which would silently mis-count latent heat crossed mid-step.

nodes.label: CHALLENGE.md (kill-shot questions, e.g. K-01, K-05, C-01, C-02, C-06)
Duffie & Beckman, Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes
Erbs, Klein & Duffie (1982), diffuse radiation fraction estimation
Kusuda & Achenbach (1965), earth temperature and thermal diffusivity
Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer
Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids
Patankar, Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow
CI workflow: verify job (typecheck, lint, format, HARD GATE, tests, energy-balance-gate)
T-01 — npm workspace root, strict TypeScript, engine package manifest
T-02 — Put the project under version control
nodes.rationale: The project had never been under version control; three thousand lines of verified engine code existed in exactly one place with no history and no undo.

nodes.label: T-03 — ESLint, Prettier, and the two boundary rules
nodes.rationale: packages/** must never import react or @prisma/client — keeps the engine runnable in a Node worker thread and in a browser; a violation is silent until the offline fallback dies on demo day.

nodes.label: T-04 — Continuous integration
nodes.rationale: The energy-balance residual is the project's cheapest, most persuasive credibility signal, and is only worth anything asserted on every commit rather than claimed in a document.

nodes.label: T-05 — The .work/ claim ledger and board.sh
nodes.rationale: LOG.md is not an atomic lock — two agents can both read [ ] and believe they own a task; .work/<ID>.md created with shell noclobber lets the filesystem arbitrate instead.

nodes.label: T-06 — Extend the shared contract with the types the rest of the build needs
nodes.rationale: Eight areas of the build need shared types that don't exist yet; adding them once, additive-only, in a frozen contract file prevents downstream tasks from inventing incompatible versions.

nodes.label: T-07 — Canonical test fixtures, including the C-01 kill-shot pair
nodes.rationale: CHALLENGE.md C-01 needs a specific insulation-vs-thermal-mass shelter pair (stone masonry vs steel+PUF) where B is the better-insulated shelter, so the comparison actually proves something about thermal mass rather than insulation alone.

nodes.label: T-72 — Cover apps/web/** in the root ESLint config
nodes.rationale: Flat ESLint config only lints files matching some block's glob; since apps/web had no matching block, npm run lint had linted zero frontend files since the app was scaffolded.

nodes.label: T-78 — Exclude test files from apps/web/tsconfig.json so npm run build survives app/api/ deletion
nodes.rationale: tsconfig's include list type-checked every .ts file including a test with a dynamic import of app/api/materials/route; deleting app/api/ broke next build's tsc step.

nodes.label: T-79 — Prettier formatting sweep (close the npm run format:check red)
nodes.rationale: format:check had been red for at least two sessions (115-212 files); no task owned Prettier formatting so nobody would fix it accidentally.

nodes.label: T-08 — Linear algebra: dense LU, Thomas, and the arrow/Schur factorisation
nodes.rationale: A dependency-free linear solver the team fully understands, so 'what solver do you use' has an answer that's a file you can open, not a library name.

nodes.label: T-09 — Envelope meshing, harmonic interfaces, composite U-value
nodes.rationale: The node chain through a wall's thickness IS the physics that makes passive design work; without it the only capacitance is the indoor air and every shelter crashes to ambient after sunset.

nodes.label: T-10 — Model assembly: node index, capacitance vector, conductance matrix
T-11 — Time integration, and the AUDIT F-1 coefficient-refresh fix
nodes.rationale: AUDIT F-1: the blueprint claimed the system matrix is constant and can be LU-factorised once, but h_o/h_r,sky/h_i all change every step; refactorising a dense LU every step is ~400x over budget, so coefficients are frozen per weather-hour instead.

nodes.label: T-12 — THE HARD GATE: analytical Test 2 (sinusoidal wave through a wall) and Test 7
nodes.rationale: If this test passes, the core solver is correct — everything else is bookkeeping; a closed-form comparison is stronger evidence than matching another program.

nodes.label: T-13 — Analytical Tests 1, 4, 6 and 8, plus the safety and validation cases
